newsitem.title: ITALY: German industry wants Italy in EMU at start - Henkel.
newsitem.headline: German industry wants Italy in EMU at start - Henkel.

text.p: German industrialists want to see Italy and Spain enter the single currency as soon as possible, the head of the Federation of German Industry (BDI) said in an Italian radio interview on Thursday.
"I am a convinced supporter of the entry of Italy and of Spain into monetary union and if possible the sooner the better," BDI President Hans-Olaf Henkel told Radio Popolare.
"Monetary union without these two countries will not be complete. And for German industry, Italy has a particular importance," he told the Milan-based private radio station by telephone from Berlin.

He was asked about weekend comments by Horst Siebert, president of the Kiel Institute of World Economics, who along with other German bankers attending the Davos Economic Forum warned of financial market turmoil if countries like Italy were allowed to help launch Europe's single currency in 1999.
"I know his reservations over certain aspects of monetary union. He thinks that countries which have economic problems can correct them by devaluation.
"In future this will not be possible, there will be other possibilities - people moving from one country to another or that salaries may be, for example, sharply reduced," Henkel said.

Referring to Friday's meeting in Bonn between Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Henkel said the two leaders had an excellent personal relationship. "I am sure we will find a solution to satisfy both countries."
Henkel said German industrialists were impressed by what Prodi had managed to achieve since becoming premier last year.

"Prodi, waving the flag of early re-entry to the European exchange rate mechanism, has succeeded in carrying out reforms. More has been done in Italy in the last 12 months than in the last 20 years - on privatisations, financing of the pensions system and discipline in public accounts," he said.

"We in Germany have the sensation that there has been a drastic change for the better in Italian economic policy. The results are there for all to see - Prodi took the lira back into the ERM, the lira is stable, Italy has improved.
"I must admit that Germany is not what it once was. We didn't manage to achieve convergence criteria last year, or the year before. For 1997 we are struggling to do so," he said.
Asked if it was true German industrialists did not have the same worries as some German bankers about Italy, Henkel replied, "Yes, that's possible."
